status: research; nothing here is read by the build. The site figures were computed on the site data of 2026-10-25 (before the parallel mid-size start and small-buyer bias fixes land) and must be recomputed at integration

design_notes.weather: the observed volumes are NOT corrected to normal weather: the no-war world had the same winters, so correcting a mild winter upward would count weather as war. Heating degree days are used to separate weather from price and policy in the EU gas shortfall (eu_gas_policy_shortfall)
design_notes.trend: observed demand already carries the pre-war trend (renewables, efficiency) and the actual economy; nothing is added. A war-driven change of trend (REPowerEU) is the policy part, carried as range
design_notes.double_counting: the price correction covers only the volume that disappeared (demand at no-war prices minus observed); the windfall line is the price on actual volumes, so the two do not overlap. The site's expected path keeps valuing fuel at the no-war price (bmul x mul), unchanged
design_notes.laundered_oil: the share is Russia's direct share (exporter or country of origin = Russia) before the war; fuel made from Russian crude in third countries was not in it, and has its own no-war baseline in the laundered part, so share x total does not count it twice. War-time totals include laundered fuel as demand, which is right: it is demand the direct share would have served. per_country_inputs gives the laundered 2021 level next to the direct flow
design_notes.origin: Eurostat energy imports are by country of origin (rerouted Russian fuel stays Russian); BACI is by exporter (consignment); Hong Kong's origin data cover gold only, and Hong Kong keeps the current method (gold transit hub)
design_notes.hubs: ARM, GEO, KAZ, KGZ, UZB, TUR, AZE, MNG, TJK, SRB, ARE, BLR and HKG keep the current method: their imports from all suppliers were reshaped by goods passing to Russia (Armenia's other goods x3.5, Azerbaijan's crude x22 by 2024)
design_notes.guard: added after the first diagnostic run, for the 2022-2026 application only (the back-test is unchanged): a product whose imports from all suppliers moved more than x3 either way against 2021 keeps held flat (data breaks: Mongolia's products x0.05 in BACI 2024, Algeria's gas, Lebanon's coal); European gas uses inland consumption, not imports (Austria's gas imports x2.6 in 2022 were storage and transit)
design_notes.years_2025_2026: BACI ends in 2024: outside Eurostat's monthly energy data, 2025-2026 hold the 2024 demand index

question: Does an observed-demand model (the country's imports of each product from all suppliers x its pre-war Russian share, corrected to no-war prices) predict purchases from Russia better than 2021 held flat?

rule.written: 2026-10-25, before any back-test result was computed
rule.unit: product x size class. Products: crude (HS 2709), oil products (2710), gas (2711), coal (2701), cereals (HS 10), fertilisers (31), metals (72-76), other goods. Size class of the product flow from Russia: the 4-year average to the origin in EUR, S under 0.1bn, M 0.1-1bn, L over 1bn; flows under EUR 10 m left out. The rest of HS 27 (coke, bitumen, electricity...) is never a candidate: it stays held flat
rule.candidate: D: the product's start level (origin year) x the importer's imports of the product from all suppliers in year t over the origin year (tonnes for the four fuel headings where the unit value is sane, else value deflated by the world unit-value index; other goods by value deflated by their world index) x the price correction (realised / expected crude price)^|elasticity| (central elasticity; expected = the IMF WEO October vintage of the origin year, no-change for the 2005-2007 origins, which have no vintage). D0 (no price correction) is a diagnostic only
rule.reference: M0: the product's origin-year level held flat (real)
rule.error: the site's cumulative error: log(sum w*actual / sum w*predicted) over H = 1..5 years, w = 1 except 8/12 for the fifth year; per origin, the mean over H1-H5 of the median absolute error
accept_if_all: accuracy: D's error is at least 15% lower than M0's at EVERY rolling origin 2005-2016 (12 origins, including the 2008 crash and the 2013/2014 Russia-shock origins), with at least 5 cases at each origin; a cell with fewer cases at any origin fails (not enough evidence)

band: D's era-calibrated 90% band for the five-year sum (H5; the to_rus_cf.json method: 5th-95th percentile x K, K the smallest factor for which two eras cover at least 90% of the third; eras 2005-09, 2010-12, 2013-16) is not wider (in log width) than M0's

placebo: D's band (built only from origins whose windows end before the placebo window, with the cell's K) covers at least 90% of the placebo errors for the war moved to 2014 (origin 2013, H5, 2014-2018; training origins up to 2008) and to 2018 (origin 2017, H4, 2018-2021; training origins up to 2013); where a cell has fewer than 10 placebo cases, the product's cases pooled over size classes are used
rule.data_sets: the four fuels are judged on Eurostat energy imports by country of origin (physical units, pipeline gas included) for the European reporters, and on CEPII BACI elsewhere; the other goods on BACI everywhere. A product passes for a country only on the data set that covers that country
rule.application: a passing product replaces 'held flat' for that product inside the country's expected path; the others keep the current method. Small flows (country total under EUR 0.1bn a year) keep the current method in the proposal. The diagnostic variant applies D to every candidate product of every country
rule.multiple_testing: 8 products x 3 size classes x 2 data sets for fuels; a chance pass is possible; every cell is reported
